messages:
ana: FYI perf-bot flagged a host-side regression in streaming tests after kernel-selector deploy :eyes:
perf-bot: [alert] 99th-latency +48% on streaming ingress (long tails)
kevin: saw the alert, digging. initial pprof points at request parsing + tokenizer hot paths
ana: attaching trimmed pprof snippet
```
# pprof flame: host_parser.go:Parse -> tokenizer.go:ScanRune
flat  32.7%  ... host_parser
flat  18.1%  ... tokenizer
```
mira: interesting — batching heuristic changed on last PR, we now prefer larger batches which increases avg seq len in host, could be queueing/kvcache churn
sam: re-ran locally with mixed short/long sequences; tokenization wall time up 2.2x for short requests when mixed in batch
kevin: likely cause: tokenizer does full unicode normalization per chunk; when chunks are small but many, syscall/allocs spike
ana: short-term workaround: route <=32 tokens to fast-path parser (no unicode normalize) and force `batch_size_limit`=16 for ingress group B
mira: also let's tweak kernel-selector: prefer small-kernel for expected seq<=64, avoids kernel warmup cost
kevin: I'll open a tiny PR for both fast-path and selector tweak, add canary in eng-runtime/staging
ana: perf-bot: please re-run streaming-job with these flags and post deltas
sam: thanks — will run runbook and post numbers here later :thumbsup:
